label: copy-phase input h (fed-back h)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, when the input token is h, i.e. the model is reading back its own output h (original token recall_idx-1 was h). It never fires in the original phase, on the delimiter, or on any other input token (1 stray activation on u). It is very weak at recall_idx 1, where the fed-back h is original token 0, and the strongest activations come early in the copy (recall_idx 2-4, especially right after the first copied token). A second h in a row (orig h h) is weaker than the first, and h fed back late or at the final step is often weak or absent, which accounts for most false positives. Simple version (phase==2 & in_tok==h): dev F1 0.86 with recall 1.0. Adding recall_idx>=2: dev P 0.90, R 0.97, F1 0.93, mass recall 0.99.

issues: The claims hold up. On dev, the feature fires 0 times in the original phase and 0 times on the delimiter. Of 69263 active steps, 69262 have input h and 1 has input u, so the single stray activation is real.

At recall_idx 1, precision is only 0.14 and mass share is 0.006, which matches 'very weak at recall_idx 1'. Mass share by recall_idx is 0.40, 0.33 and 0.15 for recall_idx 2, 3 and 4, which matches 'strongest at 2-4'.

The false positives are graded, not one separable class. With input h in the copy phase, precision is about 1.0 at recall_idx 2-4 and falls to 0.80, 0.65, 0.69 and 0.78 at recall_idx 5-8. At to_go==0 it is 0.80 (0.70 when also recall_idx>=5). When h repeats (prev_tok==h) it is 0.75, and when h appears twice in the original (in_count>=2) it is 0.72. The explanation already describes this falloff.

I found no clean variable that separates late h's that fire from late h's that don't. I checked h count, L, digits, previous token, output token and correctness: all leave late-copy precision around 0.64-0.83. These cases hold little activation mass (missed activations total 0.6% of mass on test).
Restricting further makes the score worse. Excluding late final steps gives test F1 0.888, and capping at recall_idx<=6 gives test F1 0.898, both below the original 0.929.
I reproduced the reported test scores exactly: precision 0.895, recall 0.965, F1 0.929, mass recall 0.994.
